title: RemoteTerm · MeshCore Web Terminal
author: jkingsman / RemoteTerm contributors; Seeed Studio guide
description: Run a browser-based MeshCore messaging and monitoring station on a Raspberry Pi with a XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 companion radio. View contacts and packets, exchange messages, and connect supported integrations such as MQTT.
imageAlt: RemoteTerm for MeshCore overview from the Seeed Studio setup guide.
setup: Assemble the XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 Kit, attach its antenna, and flash the matching MeshCore Serial Companion firmware.
Prepare a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W with Raspberry Pi OS and connect the radio using a USB data cable.
Install RemoteTerm using the upstream instructions, then configure the connected companion radio.
Open the browser interface on your trusted local network, configure the regional radio settings, and test channel or direct messages.
Add packet monitoring, bots, or MQTT integrations as needed. Follow the upstream access-control guidance before enabling remote access.

title: T1000-E · MeshCore Companion Relay
author: Seeed Studio / Advent Jiang
description: Use three T1000-E nodes to explore MeshCore contact sharing and temporary companion relaying. The guide compares message delivery with the middle node powered off and on; results depend on placement and radio conditions.
imageAlt: SenseCAP T1000-E devices used with the MeshCore App.
setup: Prepare three T1000-E devices with compatible MeshCore companion firmware and the MeshCore App. The guide uses firmware v1.17.1 and app v1.47.0.
Configure matching radio parameters supported by the firmware and permitted in your region.
Enable Repeat Mode only on the middle companion. Keep the two endpoint devices in normal companion mode.
Exchange contact identities with the middle node, then share the endpoint contact cards through the Public Channel.

Compare messages received at the destination with the middle node powered off and on. Contact sharing alone does not create radio coverage, and companion relaying is a temporary supplement to fixed repeaters.

title: Trail Mate · Offline Navigation on L2 Pro
author: vicliu624 / Trail Mate contributors
description: Turn Wio Tracker L2 Pro into a touchscreen handheld for offline maps, GNSS navigation, and LoRa messaging over Meshtastic or MeshCore. Board-specific firmware and setup guides are available from the project.
devices: Wio Tracker L2 Pro touchscreen model
microSD card for offline maps and stored data
imageAlt: Trail Mate tracker interface rendered with sample KML route and simulated GPS data; not a device photograph.
setup: Use the Wio Tracker L2 Pro touchscreen model and select the wio_tracker_l2 target in the project documentation.
Install the matching L2 firmware using the project browser installer or its board-specific release files.
Choose Meshtastic or MeshCore and configure your regional LoRa settings and contacts.
Prepare the offline map packages described in the navigation guide and copy them to the microSD card.
Open Tracker to use GNSS, offline maps, and route tools. Check the L2 target notes for supported peripherals and feature limits.

title: ZephCore · MeshCore on Zephyr
author: liquidraver / ZephCore contributors; logo by recrof
description: Run MeshCore-compatible firmware built on Zephyr RTOS. Published builds cover Wio Tracker L1, T1000-E, and supported XIAO variants, with companion and repeater roles plus configurable power-saving features.
devices: XIAO ESP32S3 with a compatible LoRa module
XIAO nRF52840 with a compatible LoRa module
setup: Check the supported-board list and select the exact hardware variant and companion or repeater role.
Back up your configuration before switching firmware. Settings do not carry over between stock MeshCore and ZephCore.
Use the ZephCore web flasher or download the matching published firmware. nRF52840 targets use UF2; ESP32 targets use their board-specific merged binary.
Configure regional radio settings, then pair a companion with the MeshCore app or configure a repeater through the documented CLI.
Follow the board-specific notes before enabling optional power-saving or peripheral features.

title: MeshCore Open · Images over LoRa
description: Share AI-reconstructed images over a low-bandwidth MeshCore network. MeshCore Open encodes a small representation on the sender and reconstructs a similar image on the receiver. Reconstructed details may differ from the original.
author: MeshCore Open community / Seeed Studio
setup: Install a MeshCore Open app release that supports image transmission, following the current project documentation.
Connect a compatible MeshCore node, configure the LoRa region and network, and prepare a second node as the receiver.
Enable image transmission and download the machine-learning model files in app settings.
Choose an image and send it. The receiving app reconstructs the image from the compressed representation.
Use reconstructed images for general scene awareness; they are not exact copies suitable for evidence or precise image analysis.

title: EasySkyMesh · Low-Power Mesh Firmware
description: Build low-power sensor networks with EasySkyMesh, a community firmware based on MeshCore. Add power-saving features and supported I2C sensors to Wio Tracker L1 for remote monitoring and off-grid experiments.
author: IoTThinks / EasySkyMesh community
setup: Connect Wio Tracker L1 to a computer with a USB data cable.
Download an EasySkyMesh release matching your board and installation type.
Open the MeshCore Web Flasher, choose Custom Firmware, select the file, and enter DFU mode when prompted. Flash and reboot.
Configure the regional radio settings. Companion power saving is enabled by default; repeaters and room servers require the powersaving on CLI command.
Connect supported sensors with the correct voltage and I2C wiring; follow the project sensor guide.
